findings.summary: the case added for the released-claim repair cannot fail on the defect it was added for: the fixture holds no claim that binds the path (a stopped run whose claim is released and a queued run), and held_path_blockers emits a row only when sides['holders'] is non-empty, so reinstating `side = "holders" if claim.get("binding", True) else "waiting"` leaves `held == []` true; the repair is real in the code but nothing tests it.
findings.text: follow-on: the case added for the released-claim repair cannot fail on the defect it was added for: the fixture holds no claim that binds the path (a stopped run whose claim is released and a queued run), and held_path_blockers emits a row only when sides['holders'] is non-empty, so reinstating `side = "holders" if claim.get("binding", True) else "waiting"` leaves `held == []` true; a third fixture run holding the path would make the released one appear as waiting and redden the case, as the defect did before the repair.

findings.summary: the classification assertion compares the section row against a direct call to partition_live_runs on the same pointer, and the fixture records no watcher event, so a row that derived its own classification by classify_pointer would return the same string and the assertion would still hold - the regression its docstring names is not reachable through this fixture.
findings.text: follow-on: the assertion compares the section row against a direct call to partition_live_runs on the same pointer the test handed to build_roadmap, and the fixture has no recorded watcher event, so the record-led read and a fresh classify_pointer answer coincide; a row that derived its own classification, the regression the docstring names, would leave the assertion true. A fixture carrying a recorded event for the run is the case where the two readings diverge and the assertion can fail.
